fact: UNICEF's social policy section chief said more than 500,000 vulnerable households have been registered in Niger's Registre social unifié (RSU) and now receive adapted services, with targeting to be extended to the worst-affected zones.
The article says the Registre Social Unifié (RSU), although progressing, is not yet deployed across the whole country and suffers update delays.

The Registre Social Unifié-Niger, run from the Prime Minister's office, is described as an information system holding household and individual data and delivering dashboards on social protection actions, and as the entry point for programmes.
The World Bank's PPSAS says it contributed to setting up Niger's Registre Social Unifié.
